neighbours.label: 'by' introducing the means or method by which something is done or obtained (by drilling, by tilting its body), as opposed to 'by' naming the agent of a passive
fire: The frog keeps its skin moist by hiding under wet leaves during the day.
The villagers got fresh water by digging a well behind the church.
The data were collected by interviewing three hundred nurses.
Some spiders catch fish by waiting at the edge of a pond.
The museum acquired the painting by trading two smaller works.
Desert beetles survive by trapping droplets of mist on their backs.
The prisoners escaped by tunnelling under the outer wall.
Early sailors found their position by measuring the angle of the sun.
quiet: The frog in the photograph was found by a schoolboy near the pond.
The village well was dug by the monks who lived behind the church.
The survey was designed by three senior nurses at the hospital.
The spider in the jar was caught by my younger brother.
The painting was donated by a collector who lived in Paris.
The desert beetles were described by a Dutch zoologist in 1910.
The prisoners were recaptured by guards on the outer wall.
The old map was drawn by a sailor who served on the ship.
